summary: DAY falsification pass challenged every b03 company without manufacturing bearishness. Mature names mostly have identifiable cyclicality/concentration/backlog-conversion risks that can be carried as risk rather than gates. SERV, AUR and SMR have materially stronger financing/commercialization falsifiers and should not receive survival or execution credit until capitalization is normalized by the underwriting lane; those are lane-relevant present facts, not generic future uncertainty.

materialFindings.finding: Falsifier: current record AI test demand is highly customer/geography concentrated; Q2 filing says a limited number of significant customers drive substantial test purchases and 40% of revenue was attributable to Taiwan customer sites. Robotics recovery does not remove semiconductor-cycle concentration.

Falsifier: automation recovery can be cyclical and acquisition/impairment complexity can obscure underlying economics; Sensia impairment/asbestos effects require normalized GAAP-to-operating treatment rather than headline margin extrapolation.

Falsifier: Q2 ASP declined 1% as China OEM mix rose, while fuller systems are expected to reduce gross margin because of higher hardware content. SuperVision volume growth therefore does not mechanically imply margin expansion.

Falsifier: $2.7M FY2025 revenue versus large deployment ambitions and a $100M registered direct offering makes dilution/financing dependence central. Robot count and city count are not substitutes for unit economics or self-funded scale.

Falsifier: FY2025 operating cash use around $581M against minimal revenue means commercialization can succeed technically while equity value remains financing-sensitive. DaaS asset-light intent is not yet demonstrated steady-state economics.

Falsifier: 2026 growth includes acquisition contribution and data-center order acceleration; backlog/order strength can normalize if hyperscaler electrical build schedules slip. Broad end-market strength and high margins reduce but do not eliminate this risk.
Falsifier: record backlog can mask project timing, fixed-price execution, labor and customer concentration risk; backlog must not be equated one-for-one with future margin or cash conversion.
Falsifier: a >$400M data-center award is unusually large relative to historical scale, increasing customer/project concentration and cancellation/modification sensitivity even as backlog rises.

Falsifier: nuclear/data-center contracts add duration but Calpine integration, regulatory approvals and restart execution can absorb capital and management attention; contract headlines do not remove commodity/hedge and integration risks.
Falsifier: long-duration PPAs can improve visibility while introducing counterparty, basis/hedge and asset-performance dependencies. Acquisition growth must be separated from organic fleet economics.

Falsifier: ~$20B current backlog is not homogeneous product backlog; service duration and tax-incentive assumptions can inflate superficial TAM/backlog comparisons. Backlog quality must be decomposed before confidence inflation.

Falsifier: $1.3B liquidity is materially equity-financed; 39.3M ATM shares sold for $750M gross in Q4 2025. ENTRA1/TVA remains nonbinding, so liquidity and prospective project scale cannot be scored as if internally funded contracted deployment.

gatingGaps: current fully diluted capitalization and financing runway required to quantify dilution/survival risk
current fully diluted capitalization/runway normalization required for financing-risk treatment
fully diluted capitalization after Q4 ATM and explicit nonbinding-project treatment required before survival/commercialization confidence

contradictions: TER's record AI-driven growth coexists with explicit limited-customer concentration; neither fact cancels the other.
SMR's strong cash balance coexists with material recent dilution and nonbinding flagship deployment evidence.
unknowns: No canonical live crowding/short-interest feed was required or fabricated; absence does not block baseline treatment.
peerRequests: Company-underwriting: close SERV/AUR/SMR capitalization denominators; Chief should preserve backlog-quality caveats for PWR/POWL/BE rather than converting them to binary blockers.
